priorities.title: Prompt contract and prefix discipline
priorities.summary: Keep stable instructions, tool definitions, and reusable context ahead of the variable tail.
priorities.why: This is the highest leverage path for cache hit rate, latency, cost, and model consistency.

priorities.title: Cache diagnostics and regression gates
priorities.summary: Expose cache key, cache mode, hit rate, and changed prefix fields in the operator flow.
priorities.why: Operators need miss explanations at the same place they inspect runtime status.

priorities.title: TUI simplification and inspector split
priorities.summary: Keep the default surface conversation-first and push dense runtime detail into inspector views.
priorities.why: The product must feel like a chat-first operator surface, not a kernel dashboard.

priorities.title: Boundary hardening across Swarm, Symphony, and Gateway
priorities.summary: Align naming, routing, and docs so each surface stays in its own lane.
priorities.why: Boundary drift creates product confusion and makes Gateway look like a second UI.

priorities.title: Narrow LSP productization
priorities.summary: Keep the local semantic service focused on the operations the product already exposes.
priorities.why: The LSP should support the operator surface, not grow into a broad language platform.

priorities.title: Cross-surface health signals
priorities.summary: Unify cache, TUI, Symphony, and LSP signals only after the main surface is stable.
priorities.why: This is useful, but it should not distract from the core prompt and TUI work.
